To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed agent is capable to interact with elderly in a natural way, to provide them with information on basic care and healthcare, and to retrieve and present multimedia content from the web in a multimodal fashion.

the agent is capable of conducting a conversation on basic care and healthcare with an elderly person, and that it has a good performance in terms of the accuracy of the retrieved content from the web.

(i) the presented agent has the potential to become a useful tool for the care of elderly people, (ii) it can be used as a training tool for healthcare professionals, (iii) its multimodality is an important factor that can increase its effectiveness, (iv) it can be extended to other domains, such as the tourism domain, (v) it is an important step towards the development of intelligent agents with social competence and human interaction capabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of an agent capable to conduct a conversation with elderly people, to provide information about their health condition and to support them in the process of self-diagnosis and self-medication.
developing a knowledge-based agent capable of human-like interaction in the context of basic care and healthcare for the elderly and migrants.
the design of a conversational agent with a human-like ability to communicate and interact socially with elderly and migrants in a culturally and linguistically appropriate way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed agent has the potential to become a useful tool in the context of elderly care and health care, especially in the context of migrant and multicultural communities.

the presented agent is an intelligent embodied conversation system with a knowledge base of basic care and healthcare information that is able to interact in natural language and multimodal communication with the elderly and migrants.

the agent presented in this paper is able to have a conversation on a topic of interest to the user, using a multimodal communication, including speech, facial expressions, and gestures, and is able to adapt the conversation to the user's needs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an ontology-based dialogue manager, a social competence model, a social emotion model and a multimodal communication analysis module.

the agent can have a natural language conversation in English with the user and can also communicate in other languages using the multimodal communication analysis module, and it can retrieve multimedia content related to the conversation topic using a web search module.
we have a system that can be used for conducting a dialogue in the basic care domain and can be extended to the healthcare domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a dialogue system for a social agent can be built on a knowledge-based architecture that is based on a formal representation of knowledge about the domain, the user and the agent, and that can be extended to include cultural and emotional knowledge and reasoning.

a knowledge-based agent is needed for a more effective communication between elderly and migrants with the healthcare providers and that the agent can be enhanced with a set of social and emotional competences to be able to communicate with the target population.

the integration of a search engine and a multimedia content analysis module into a conversational system is a challenging task, but it is possible to achieve good performance in terms of content retrieval and multimodal generation.
